You are implementing one slice in the DeepSeek Harness monorepo (a pnpm workspace). Read /home/user/deepseek-harness/AGENTS.md, packages/AGENTS.md, docs/testing.md and .agents/notes/README.md in YOUR worktree before changing anything; every rule there binds you (per-file 100% coverage, JSDoc on exports, typed events by declaration merging, "misconfiguration fails loud", bilingual Agent Notes). You work in an isolated git worktree created for you; commit there and report the branch and commit SHA. Do not push. Another agent is concurrently rewriting `packages/llm/llm-claude-code` in its own worktree: do not touch that package.

# The slice: an external implementer runs the model the cell names

## Problem (established, do not redo)

The environment runner (`packages/improvement/environment-runner/src/index.ts`, method `delegate`, around line 1020) starts an out-of-process implementer through `implementer.subagents.start(provider, { prompt, parent, signal, label? })` and records `environment/delegation { attempt, provider, runId, stopReason, structured?, usage? }`. The cell's model (`request.model`, e.g. `{ provider: 'claude-code', model: 'sonnet' }`, stamped on `environment/run` and shown on every observatory row and scorekeeper fact) is not forwarded: the Claude Code subagent provider (`packages/subagent/subagent-claude-code`) spawns the product with no `--model`, so every delegated cell runs the installation's default model while its facts claim the arm's model. A fleet plan `{ models: [{ provider: 'claude-code', model: 'sonnet' }], implementer: { kind: 'subagent', provider: 'claude-code' } }` therefore produces mislabeled measurements, and a paired experiment whose candidate arm names a subagent implementer cannot compare like with like. Evidence: a running fleet's product processes show `claude --output-format stream-json … --permission-mode acceptEdits --no-session-persistence` with no model flag (`pgrep -af claude`), and no cell session log holds the product model anywhere.

## Design

1. The subagent seam's start request (`packages/subagent/subagent/src/types.ts`, the options `start(provider, …)` takes) gains an optional `model?: string`: the provider-specific model identifier the child must run. Document it at the Service Definition as the seam's contract: a provider that receives a `model` it cannot honor rejects the start with a coded error (name it in the seam's error taxonomy, e.g. `SUBAGENT_MODEL_UNSUPPORTED`); a provider never silently runs another model.
2. `packages/subagent/subagent-claude-code`: forward `model` to the product (the SDK `model` option / `--model` flag, whichever this provider uses; look at `src/run.ts`, `src/process.ts`, `src/index.ts`, `src/types.ts`), in both its plain mode and its bridge mode. Record the model the child reports in its `system`/`init` message (field `model`, e.g. a full product model id) on whatever this provider already records per run so the parent can log it; if the provider records nothing per run today, expose it on the run result (`result.structured` is model output, do not overload it; add a typed field such as `result.model` or `run.reportedModel`, whichever fits the seam's existing result type; check how the program department's delegation records the same facts so the two stay symmetrical).
3. Other providers (`subagent-codex`, `subagent-acp`, `subagent-dsh-sdk`, the in-process providers): forward when the provider has an equivalent (Codex has a model flag; ACP may not), otherwise reject a start that carries `model` with the coded error. In-process providers that run on the harness's own LLM seam may honor it by selecting the named model on their child session's route if that is a one-line matter, otherwise reject; do what the seam's existing code makes natural, and document each provider's answer in its README.
4. The runner's `delegate()` forwards `model: request.model.model` for a subagent implementer and records on `environment/delegation` both the requested `model` (the cell's `{ provider, model }` is already on `environment/run`, so record only what is new: the model the child reported, as `reportedModel?: string`). Extend the event's JSDoc (`@mode`, `@param` for each payload field) and every invariant, projection, scorekeeper fact, trajectory record, or observatory column that folds delegation records if one of them should surface the reported model (at minimum the scorekeeper fact of a delegated session should be able to tell "requested sonnet, child reported claude-sonnet-…"; keep the change minimal but truthful). Adding an optional field to an existing event payload is additive; do not bump `SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION` unless the repository's session-log version mechanism note says an additive optional field requires it (read `.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-08-10-session-log-version-mechanism.md`).
5. The program ledger (`packages/improvement/program`) delegates departments to external implementers the same way (`program/delegation`); apply the same forwarding there if its department spec names a model, otherwise leave a one-line Known Limitation.
6. The bench composition `examples/headless-agent/tests/fixtures/proving-ground-bench/cordis.yml` and its drivers need no change if the plan's `models[].model` values (`opus`, `sonnet`, `haiku`) are aliases the product accepts; confirm by reading the `llm-claude-code` catalog in that file (`productModel` aliases) and state in the runner README that a fleet naming a subagent implementer must name models the provider accepts verbatim.

## Deliverables

- Code and tests in the touched packages with per-file 100% coverage (`pnpm run test:coverage` scoped as docs/testing.md describes); the subagent-claude-code package has keyless tests with a fake product process and real-product e2e tests that self-skip without the `claude` CLI: extend both (the `claude` CLI on PATH is authenticated, run the real ones and report). Add a runner unit test asserting the forwarded `model` and the recorded `reportedModel`, and a loader-booted e2e assertion where the existing external-implementer fixture already runs (search `examples/` for `environment/delegation`).
- Keyless snapshot: if any snapshot transcript shows `environment/delegation`, re-record it per docs/testing.md.
- READMEs: subagent seam (the new request field and the rejection contract), each provider, environment runner (delegation record fields), scorekeeper/observatory if touched.
- One Agent Note `.agents/notes/proposed/architecture/2026-09-07-delegated-implementer-model.md` in the enforced format (line 1 `# Agent Note: <title>`, line 3 `Status: proposed`, line 5 the language switch line sibling notes use, sections `## Problem`, `## Proposal`, bespoke sections, `## Alternatives considered`, `## Acceptance criteria`, `## Risks`), with its `.zh.md` translation and `.i18n.yaml` recorded by `pnpm run verify-translation-pairing --write <en path>`.
- `pnpm run typecheck`, `pnpm run lint`, `pnpm run duplication`, `pnpm run hygiene`, `pnpm run doc-sync` all green; report exactly which commands you ran and their results.

## Commit

Commit on the worktree branch. No model identifiers of the assistant in code, docs, or commit messages (product model aliases such as `sonnet` that already appear in the repository are fine). Every commit message ends with exactly these two trailer lines:

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01HEXjzxR7CyMizem5kFAB4C

The lefthook pre-commit hook runs staged lint, pairing, and whitespace checks; fix what it reports, never bypass it. Never commit credentials. Report at the end: branch, SHA(s), commands run with results, open questions.

# AGENTS.md

DeepSeek Harness is a plugin-based agent harness on vendored Cordis: **everything is a plugin**. Read [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) before changing `packages/`; follow [docs/AGENTS.md](docs/AGENTS.md) for documentation.

## Pre-release stance: foundation over blast radius

**Remove this section at the first tagged release.** With no external consumers, prefer the correct foundation over compatibility shims: rename or repackage freely and update every reference together. Backends reject old on-disk formats. SQLite uses monotonic `SCHEMA_VERSION`; `dsh-session` keeps `SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION` at `0` without a compatibility promise.

## Repository layout

```
vendor/      Vendored Cordis source — manifest + sync procedure in vendor/README.md
packages/    @deepseek-ai/dsh-<pkg> workspaces at packages/<group>/<pkg>/
  core/        product API spine: session, system-prompt, tools, agent, agent-loop
  api/         Remote BFF assembly and Typert RPC gateway
  typert/      type graph generator, loader, and runtime registry
  llm/         LLM capability: Service Definition/Consumer + DeepSeek providers
  e2b/         E2B POC: sandbox + FS/subprocess adapters
  shell/        bash capability: Service Definition + local/pwsh providers + shell Consumers
  subprocess/  subprocess capability + local process-tree provider
  terminal/         persistent sessions
  fs/          filesystem capability + policy
  lsp/         language-server capability
  skill/       skill provider registry + local impl + catalog/loader tool
  web/         web capability: Service Definition + search/fetch providers + tool Consumer
  compaction/     compaction capability + basic provider
  context/     request-context plugins
  subagent/    subagent capability: Service Definition + providers + delegation Consumers
  bundle/      installable dsh --profile patch-layer bundles
  workflow/    workflow capability + worker-thread provider + tool Consumer
  todo/        todo_write tool
  plan/        plan mode as logged state
  preset/      per-session agent composition from preset cordis.yml files
  guard/       loop-hygiene, tool-timeout, session-budget plugins
  self-modification/  the agent inspects/mounts its own plugins
  hooks/       Claude Code/Codex hook bridges + wire-protocol library
  session/     durable session data: persistence, projection, titles, telemetry
  identity/    anonymous identity
  settings/    user-settings capability + file provider
  credentials/ credential-reference capability + env/.env provider
  acp/         automation-only Agent Client Protocol server
  interaction/ approval/interaction capabilities, permission, commands, ask-user
  boot/        shared app-bin glue
  sdk/         JSON-RPC protocol, server, and TypeScript client
  examples/    demo bundles (agent-spine + CLI/ACP/JSON-RPC bins)
  support/     dev/test infrastructure
  util/        zero-dependency utilities
python/      Python SDK and bundled runtime (see python/README.md)
native/      @deepseek-ai/node-addon-landlock-run source of record (see native/README.md)
examples/    Runnable cordis.yml leaves over packages/examples bundles (see examples/AGENTS.md)
.agents/     Agent workflows and Agent Notes (`notes/`)
docs/        architecture, generated catalogs, postmortems, cookbook (see docs/AGENTS.md)
scripts/     repo gates and generators
website/     VitePress projection of selected bilingual docs/ sources
data/        this repository's own transcripts, runs, knowledge packs (see data/README.md)
```

Package groups: [packages/README.md](packages/README.md).

## Commands

```sh
pnpm install            # pnpm workspaces, node ^22.19 || >=24
pnpm run clean           # remove build outputs and residue of deleted packages
pnpm run test           # vitest unit tests
pnpm run test:coverage  # CI coverage gate: per-file 100% on packages/*/*/src
pnpm run test:e2e       # real-API tests; self-skip without DEEPSEEK_API_KEY
pnpm run test:snapshot  # keyless ACP/headless replay vs expected outputs; filter: -t <name>
pnpm run test:snapshot:record  # re-record expected outputs (needs key)
pnpm run typecheck
pnpm run lint
pnpm run duplication    # cross-file TypeScript clone detection
pnpm run build          # tsc emits lib/types, tsdown bundles runtime
pnpm run hygiene        # knip + publint + workspace constraints + NodeNext consumer check
pnpm run check:windows-wine  # ONLY when diagnosing a known Windows failure (needs wine); CI owns it
pnpm run doc-sync       # all documentation gates; leaf list in scripts/run-gates.ts
pnpm run website:build  # VitePress build (doubles as dead-link check)
pnpm dsh --profile headless "task"  # run one task from source (needs DEEPSEEK_API_KEY)
pnpm run demo:cordis    # the agent modifies its own runtime (needs key)
pnpm run demo:acp       # ACP automation server (needs DEEPSEEK_API_KEY)
```

### Host sandbox failures

When `gh`, `pnpm`, build, test, or generator commands fail because the agent sandbox blocks credentials, network, IPC, file watching, or nested `sandbox-exec`, retry unchanged with the narrowest host escalation before diagnosing authentication or project failure. Require sandbox evidence; never bypass genuine test failures or the product sandbox under test.

### Run relevant checks locally

Run checks before pushes via [dsh-pre-push-checks](.agents/skills/dsh-pre-push-checks/SKILL.md); report only commands run. After `gh stack sync`, validate immediately; merge only after checks pass.

- Match evidence to the surface: focused tests for behavior, snapshots for model or user output, `doc-sync` for docs, build/hygiene and built smokes for published paths, real-API e2e for providers.
- Never default to the full suite or repeat a passing check for commit or push. CI owns exhaustive coverage and the platform matrix; rehearse all locally only by explicit request, for CI diagnosis, or an irreducibly repository-wide change.
- `test:coverage`, not `test`, is the CI coverage gate ([why](docs/testing.md)).

## Secrets / .env

Real-API tests and demos read `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`, optional `DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL`, and root `.env`. cordis.yml allows `!!js` (never `!js`) under plugin `config` and entry `disabled`; other metadata stays literal, so conditional composition also uses overlays ([primer](docs/cordis-primer.md#loader-configuration)). Never commit credentials. CI e2e skips without a key; [testing.md](docs/testing.md) owns key policy.

## Conventions

- Every npm package is `@deepseek-ai/dsh-<name>`; vendored packages are rescoped ([mapping](docs/rescope.md)) and `private: true`. `@deepseek-ai/cordis` is a peerDependency (+ dev) of every harness package.
- ESM everywhere (`"type": "module"`). Use package names across packages and `.ts` in local relative imports. Config subprocesses run built `lib/` under plain Node; source regressions use their declared launcher ([testing policy](docs/testing.md#test-subprocess-launch-modes)). The `dsh` CLI source launch runs through tsx's ESM-only hook (`node --import tsx/esm`); modules it reaches must stay ESM (no CJS-only exports) — Node's native TypeScript modes are unavailable across the engines range ([source-launch contract](.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-29-dsh-source-launch-tsx-esm.md)). Raw/Web `cordis.yml` bare plugins must appear in their resolver manifest's `dependencies`; `verify-cordis-config` enforces it.
- **Registrations are effects**: every contribution goes through `ctx.effect()` / `ctx.on()`; a registry's `register()` returns the disposer.
- **Runtime invariants assert owned relationships.** Check authoritative event streams or mutable data, not service or method presence, plugin metadata or effects, or fixed pure examples. Without a plausible relationship, an explained empty companion is correct ([package invariant rules](packages/AGENTS.md)).
- **Typed events use declaration merging** and merge-extensible maps. Event JSDoc needs `@mode` and payload `@param`; scoped keys absent from payloads need `@dshScopeScan unsupported`. Public service methods document parameters and non-void returns. A `SessionEventMap` member is required-on-read by default — builds that do not know its type refuse the log unless the event carries the envelope's `ignorable: true`; only structural format changes bump `SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION` ([mechanism](.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-08-10-session-log-version-mechanism.md)).
- **Switch on discriminant tags.** Closed unions end in `assertNever`; merge-extensible unions fall through a documented default.
- **Waterfall listeners MUST call `next()`** to delegate; returning without it short-circuits the chain ([semantics](docs/cordis-primer.md#cordis-waterfall-semantics)).
- **Model-visible ⟺ logged**: anything that reaches a model request must be reconstructable from the session log; a new model-visible input requires a session event.
- **Plugins, not loop changes**: new behavior goes on documented extension points; changing `agent-loop` requires updating docs/architecture.md.
- **A capability seam comprises Service Definition / Service Provider / Consumer roles.** It is complete, never one role; split only when roles evolve independently ([glossary](docs/glossary.md#capability-seam)).
- **Prefer maintained dependencies over hand-rolling** when they genuinely delete owned code and tests ([policy](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-07-26-dependencies-over-hand-rolling.md)).
- **Explicit > implicit at package boundaries**: defaulting is an explicit `resolve(request): Spec` step in the owning implementation, never a hidden `?? default` inside `run()` (the `dsh-shell` request/spec split is the template).
- **No hardcoded tunables in plugins**: deployment-varying choices are validated `Config` fields changeable from cordis.yml; a `DEFAULT_*` constant or test hook is not configurability. Protocol constants, external specs, and security invariants stay fixed.
- **Misconfiguration fails loud** at load when self-contained, otherwise at the earliest resolvable point; never silently skip a missing referent.

# AGENTS.md

DeepSeek Harness is a plugin-based agent harness on vendored Cordis: **everything is a plugin**. Read [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) before changing `packages/`; follow [docs/AGENTS.md](docs/AGENTS.md) for documentation.

## Pre-release stance: foundation over blast radius

**Remove this section at the first tagged release.** With no external consumers, prefer the correct foundation over compatibility shims: rename or repackage freely and update every reference together. Backends reject old on-disk formats. SQLite uses monotonic `SCHEMA_VERSION`; `dsh-session` keeps `SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION` at `0` with no compatibility promise.

## Repository layout

```
vendor/      Vendored Cordis source — manifest + sync procedure in vendor/README.md
packages/    @deepseek-ai/dsh-<pkg> workspaces at packages/<group>/<pkg>/
  core/        product API spine: session, system-prompt, tools, agent, agent-loop
  api/         Remote BFF assembly and Typert RPC gateway
  typert/      type graph generator, loader, and runtime registry
  llm/         LLM capability: Service Definition/Consumer + DeepSeek providers
  e2b/         E2B POC: sandbox + FS/subprocess adapters
  shell/        bash capability: Service Definition + local/pwsh providers + shell Consumers
  subprocess/  subprocess capability + local process-tree provider
  terminal/         persistent sessions
  fs/          filesystem capability + policy
  lsp/         language-server capability
  skill/       skill provider registry + local impl + catalog/loader tool
  web/         web capability: Service Definition + search/fetch providers + tool Consumer
  compaction/     compaction capability + basic provider
  context/     request-context plugins
  subagent/    subagent capability: Service Definition + providers + delegation Consumers
  bundle/      installable dsh --profile patch-layer bundles
  workflow/    workflow capability + worker-thread provider + tool Consumer
  todo/        todo_write tool
  plan/        plan mode as logged state
  preset/      per-session agent composition from preset cordis.yml files
  guard/       loop-hygiene + tool-timeout plugins
  self-modification/  the agent inspects/mounts its own plugins
  hooks/       Claude Code/Codex hook bridges + wire-protocol library
  session/     durable session data: persistence, projection, titles, telemetry
  identity/    anonymous identity
  settings/    user-settings capability + file provider
  credentials/ credential-reference capability + env/.env provider
  acp/         automation-only Agent Client Protocol server
  interaction/ approval/interaction capabilities, permission, commands, ask-user
  boot/        shared app-bin glue
  sdk/         JSON-RPC protocol, server, and TypeScript client
  examples/    demo bundles (agent-spine + CLI/ACP/JSON-RPC bins)
  support/     dev/test infrastructure
  util/        zero-dependency utilities
python/      Python SDK and bundled runtime (see python/README.md)
native/      @deepseek-ai/node-addon-landlock-run source of record (see native/README.md)
examples/    Runnable cordis.yml leaves over packages/examples bundles (see examples/AGENTS.md)
.agents/     Agent workflows and Agent Notes (`notes/`)
docs/        architecture, generated catalogs, postmortems, cookbook (see docs/AGENTS.md)
scripts/     repo gates and generators
website/     VitePress projection of selected bilingual docs/ sources
```

Package groups: [packages/README.md](packages/README.md).

## Commands

```sh
pnpm install            # pnpm workspaces, node ^22.19 || >=24
pnpm run clean           # remove build outputs and safe residue from deleted packages
pnpm run test           # vitest unit tests
pnpm run test:coverage  # CI coverage gate: per-file 100% on packages/*/*/src
pnpm run test:e2e       # real-API tests; self-skip without DEEPSEEK_API_KEY
pnpm run test:snapshot  # keyless ACP/headless replay vs expected outputs; filter: -t <name>
pnpm run test:snapshot:record  # re-record expected outputs (needs key)
pnpm run typecheck
pnpm run lint
pnpm run duplication    # cross-file TypeScript clone detection
pnpm run build          # tsc emits lib/types, tsdown bundles runtime
pnpm run hygiene        # knip + publint + workspace constraints + NodeNext consumer check
pnpm run check:windows-wine  # ONLY when diagnosing a known Windows failure (needs wine); CI owns this signal
pnpm run doc-sync       # all documentation gates; leaf list in scripts/run-gates.ts
pnpm run website:build  # VitePress build (doubles as dead-link check)
pnpm dsh --profile headless "task"  # run one task from source (needs DEEPSEEK_API_KEY)
pnpm run demo:cordis    # the agent modifies its own runtime (needs key)
pnpm run demo:acp       # ACP automation server (needs DEEPSEEK_API_KEY)
```

### Host sandbox failures

When required `gh`, `pnpm`, build, test, or generator commands fail because the agent sandbox blocks credentials, network, IPC, file watching, or nested `sandbox-exec`, retry unchanged with the narrowest host escalation before diagnosing authentication or project failure. Require sandbox evidence; never bypass genuine test failures or the product sandbox under test.

### Run relevant checks locally

Run checks before pushes via [dsh-pre-push-checks](.agents/skills/dsh-pre-push-checks/SKILL.md); report only commands run. After `gh stack sync`, validate immediately; do not merge before checks pass.

- Match evidence to the surface: focused tests for behavior, snapshots for model or user output, `doc-sync` for docs, build/hygiene and built smokes for published paths, and real-API e2e for provider behavior.
- Never default to the full suite or repeat a passing check for commit or push. CI owns exhaustive coverage and the platform matrix; rehearse all locally only by explicit request, for CI diagnosis, or for an irreducibly repository-wide change.
- `test:coverage`, not `test`, is the CI coverage gate ([why](docs/testing.md)).

## Secrets / .env

Real-API tests and demos read `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`, optional `DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL`, and root `.env`. cordis.yml allows `!!js` (never `!js`) under plugin `config` and entry `disabled`; other metadata stays literal, so conditional composition also uses overlays ([primer](docs/cordis-primer.md#loader-configuration)). Never commit credentials. CI e2e skips without a key; [testing.md](docs/testing.md) owns key policy.

## Conventions

- Every npm package is `@deepseek-ai/dsh-<name>`; vendored packages are rescoped ([mapping](docs/rescope.md)) and `private: true`. `@deepseek-ai/cordis` is a peerDependency (+ dev) of every harness package.
- ESM everywhere (`"type": "module"`). Use package names across packages and `.ts` in local relative imports. Config subprocesses run built `lib/` under plain Node; source regressions use their declared launcher ([testing policy](docs/testing.md#test-subprocess-launch-modes)). The `dsh` CLI source launch runs through tsx's ESM-only hook (`node --import tsx/esm`); modules it reaches must stay ESM (no CJS-only exports) — Node's native TypeScript modes are unavailable across the engines range ([source-launch contract](.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-29-dsh-source-launch-tsx-esm.md)). Raw/Web `cordis.yml` bare plugins must appear in their resolver manifest's `dependencies`; `verify-cordis-config` enforces it.
- **Registrations are effects**: every contribution goes through `ctx.effect()` / `ctx.on()`; a registry's `register()` returns the disposer.
- **Runtime invariants assert owned relationships.** Check authoritative event streams or mutable data, not service or method presence, plugin metadata or effects, or fixed pure examples. Without a plausible relationship, an explained empty companion is correct ([package invariant rules](packages/AGENTS.md)).
- **Typed events use declaration merging** and merge-extensible maps. Event JSDoc needs `@mode` and payload `@param`; scoped keys absent from payloads need `@dshScopeScan unsupported`. Public service methods document parameters and non-void returns. A `SessionEventMap` member is required-on-read by default — builds that do not know its type refuse the log unless the event carries the envelope's `ignorable: true`; only structural format changes bump `SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION` ([mechanism](.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-08-10-session-log-version-mechanism.md)).
- **Switch on discriminant tags.** Closed unions end in `assertNever`; merge-extensible unions fall through a documented default.
- **Waterfall listeners MUST call `next()`** to delegate; returning without it short-circuits the chain ([semantics](docs/cordis-primer.md#cordis-waterfall-semantics)).
- **Model-visible ⟺ logged**: anything that reaches a model request must be reconstructable from the session log; a new model-visible input requires a session event.
- **Plugins, not loop changes**: new behavior goes on documented extension points; changing `agent-loop` requires updating docs/architecture.md.
- **A capability seam comprises Service Definition / Service Provider / Consumer roles.** It is complete, never one role; split only when roles evolve independently ([glossary](docs/glossary.md#capability-seam)).
- **Prefer maintained dependencies over hand-rolling** when they genuinely delete owned code and tests ([policy](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-07-26-dependencies-over-hand-rolling.md)).
- **Explicit > implicit at package boundaries**: defaulting is an explicit `resolve(request): Spec` step in the owning implementation, never a hidden `?? default` inside `run()` (the `dsh-shell` request/spec split is the template).
- **No hardcoded tunables in plugins**: deployment-varying choices are validated `Config` fields changeable from cordis.yml; a `DEFAULT_*` constant or test hook is not configurability. Protocol constants, external specs, and security invariants stay fixed.
- **Misconfiguration fails loud** at load when self-contained, otherwise at the earliest resolvable point; never silently skip a missing referent.
- **Opaque cross-boundary ids are branded** (`Branded<B>` from `dsh-brand`), never bare `string`.
- **Trust TypeScript at typed same-process boundaries.** Do not add runtime validation, fallback behavior, or hostile-input tests solely for values the static interface requires; validate at parser/config, queued, model/tool JSON, durable/file, worker, process, and wire boundaries.
- **Source plane vs artifact plane, never mixed.** Static gates and tests resolve workspace imports through tsconfig `paths` to `src` and pass on a clean tree; gates consuming built `lib/` declare that dependency ([layout](docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
- **Keep compiler faces explicit.** Each package uses one aggregate except `api/remotes`; repo-wide programs seed a face config, never the root solution ([layout](docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
- **An empty `catch` names what it swallows** and why nothing else can reach it; keep the `try` to one statement.
- Do not comment on facts obvious from code.
- **Prefer symmetry for parallel values**; unexplained asymmetry usually signals a missed extraction.
- **Tests describe behavior, not correctness.** Change obsolete behavior with its tests; explain why in the PR.
- **Non-trivial changes MUST include an Agent Note in the same PR;** only mechanical/local edits are exempt ([scope](.agents/notes/README.md#when-to-write-one)). Archived notes are frozen: never edit or treat them as current authority ([archive policy](.agents/notes/README.md#archiving-and-deletion)).
- **Testing policy** — [docs/testing.md](docs/testing.md). Every non-trivial model- or product-user-visible behavior change adds or updates a keyless snapshot through a real runnable example in the same PR; package tests, e2e-only assertions, and mock-only fixtures do not substitute for the assembled application transcript. Fixtures must replay on macOS/Linux; fix fixtures, not normalizers.
- **A tool's UI render intent is part of its design**, decided up front (`generic`/`terminal`/`diff`, `locations`); presentation methods are pure functions of `args` ([cookbook](docs/cookbook/adding-a-tool.md)).
- **Plan unit, e2e, and snapshot coverage** for capability seams, lifecycle paths, and transcript output; include missing snapshot-harness support in the same change.
- **Choose PR history deliberately.** Split independent changes; fix the introducing PR before propagation. Standalone PRs and official stacks may merge-forward or rebase after review. Rewrites use `--force-with-lease`, abort on remote movement, never raw `--force`; an in-progress merge-forward preserves its checkpoint before taking a newer base ([rationale](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-08-02-native-github-stacks-and-optional-rebases.md)).
- **Labels:** one PR `kind/*`, all material `area/*`, and native Issue Type ([taxonomy](.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-08-08-unified-github-label-taxonomy.md)).
- TODO markers: `FIXME`/`TODO`/`XXX` by urgency ([semantics](docs/development.md)).
- Files end with exactly one trailing newline; `git diff --cached --check` (pre-commit) gates it.

## Defensive patterns

Read [docs/defensive-patterns.md](docs/defensive-patterns.md) before lifecycle, concurrency, subprocess, or teardown work.

## Type safety and documentation

Everything compiles under `strict: true` with `noImplicitAny`; every remaining `any` explains why narrowing is infeasible. Every module and export has concise JSDoc for its non-obvious contract; function-like exports include `@param`/`@returns`, as enforced by `verify-export-jsdoc`. Heritage-declared members, plugin-protocol slots, and constructors keep their docs at the declaring Service Definition, protocol, or class.

Comments and docs state complete contracts and context, not reasoning transcripts. Use direct, concrete terms. Do not use metaphors. Before writing `contract`, `boundary`, or `shape`, ask whether a more exact term names the subject: write `response fields`, `JSON validation`, or `ESM exports` instead of `response shape`, `validation boundary`, or `module shape`. Keep `contract` for preconditions, postconditions, invariants, compatibility promises, and other obligations that callers, callees, implementers, providers, producers, or consumers rely on. Keep a literal process, wire, security, transaction, or lifecycle boundary. Do not narrate control flow or tests, preserve review history, or restate code. Keep behavior, failure, timing, ownership, and safe-use facts; link the rationale. Use [dsh-prose-standard](.agents/skills/dsh-prose-standard/SKILL.md) for decisions. Wire mechanically checkable invariants into an executed top-level gate and prove each changed acceptance path rejects an invalid case. Use narrow, justified exceptions instead of disabling a rule globally.

Docs accompany every code change: update affected README and JSDoc contracts together. Routine bilingual work follows [docs/AGENTS.md](docs/AGENTS.md); only explicit user invocation may run `dsh-translate-docs`. Current-state prose, one physical line per paragraph, one home per fact, and word budgets live there.

## Editing these instructions

# AGENTS.md — Harness Packages

These package-specific rules supplement the repo-wide [conventions](../AGENTS.md#conventions).

- **Plugin exports:** service packages default-export their service class; function plugins named-export `name` / `inject` / `Config` / `apply` and have no default export. Mixing the forms makes the Loader discard the function plugin's namespace ([postmortem](../docs/postmortem/0001-acp-default-export-drops-inject.md)).
- **Optional services use `ctx.get(name)`.** Reserve `ctx.<name>` for declared injections; the property proxy is topology-sensitive, while strict `ctx.get` reads the global service store ([postmortem](../docs/postmortem/0001-acp-default-export-drops-inject.md)).
- **Product-visible plugins require a non-unit REAL-composition test.** Hand-built `ctx.plugin(...)` suites are insufficient. Boot test-only `cordis.yml` through the Loader and app/process; mock only external services or nondeterministic inputs and assert model-visible, durable, or user-visible output. Keep opt-ins out of shipped defaults. [Policy](../docs/testing.md).
- **Initiator-owned private chains derive, then capture.** Under `ctx.agents.withInitiator()`, recover the Agent at each orchestration entry, derive `agent.session`, and let operation-local helpers close over it. Keep `Agent` and `Session` explicit at lifecycle, session-log, service, authority, worker/process, persistence, and wire interfaces; do not widen a leaf helper from `Session` to `Context` merely to hide a parameter ([rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-15-agent-initiator-scope.md)).
- **Represent one asynchronous operation with one lifecycle controller or transaction.** Separate readiness, cancellation, disposal, reservation, or sentinel state requires an independent owner or settlement point; otherwise fold it while preserving rollback, callback containment, and quiescence.
- **Design Service Definitions for all current Consumers.** Keep tool-schema, Loader, UI, transport, and provider-specific behavior in the Consumer or provider; do not let one Consumer dictate the service contract ([capability-seam rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-06-13-capability-seams.md)). Inverse smell: a public service method with one internal caller — pass a private capability closure instead (`RunCodeBridgeOptions`).
- **Require a current owner and need.** Tie each abstraction, state machine, option, defensive copy, and compatibility path to a current contract or production consumer, and keep behavior in its owning plugin or service.
- **Require evidence for public choices.** Configurability does not justify an unsupported default, public operation set, format, or imported external concept. Use current-consumer evidence or relevant prior art; otherwise require an explicit value or defer the choice.
- **Write model-facing contracts from the model's perspective.** Prompts, tool schemas, results, and diagnostics contain only task-relevant concepts, not UI, transport, or implementation vocabulary. Pin stable model-visible text verbatim and dynamic behavior through snapshots or end-to-end coverage.
- **Enforce a decision in the operation that makes it.** Schema omission, prompt filtering, facades, wrappers, and listener order are not enforcement when direct or alternate callers can bypass them; test denial through the executor.
- **Publish state only at its commit point.** Emit each notification and update derived state only after the operation succeeds; derive caches, prompts, UI echoes, replay, and query views from one authoritative source.
- **Apply bounds to the complete result.** Enforce byte, token, item, and time limits where the complete emitted or retained value, including wrappers and metadata, is known; test tiny and exact limits, oversized single chunks, and multibyte byte limits.
- **Registry contributions prove disposal** through the HMR-safety test required by [testing policy](../docs/testing.md): dispose the fiber and observe removal.
- **Every package owns `./invariant`.** Register the manifest name; check an event/data relation or give empty installers package-specific `No runtime invariant:` reasons. Generated companions, unexplained empties, and ignored reporters fail [`verify-package-invariants`](../.agents/notes/implemented/architecture/2026-07-19-package-invariant-runtime-contracts.md).

[Naming rules](../docs/cookbook/adding-a-package.md#name-the-role-that-exists):

- **Package tsconfig:** extends `tsconfig.base.json` (Client: `tsconfig.base.client.json`), uses `rootDir: src`, `outDir: lib/types`, and references each workspace dependency plus `runtime-diagnostics/invariants`; registers in exactly one aggregate. Only `api/remotes` splits for generated contracts; ordinary two-entry Client plugins do not ([layout](../docs/development.md#typescript-project-layout)).
- `src/types.ts` contains only types — no runtime code.
- Tests live at package level under `tests/`, not `src/__tests__/`.
- A package's README and JSDoc are part of the change: altered behavior (config keys, defaults, error codes, wire fields) updates them in the same commit. `doc-sync` gates what it can; apply [dsh-prose-standard](../.agents/skills/dsh-prose-standard/SKILL.md) for complete, concise prose and verify accuracy against code.
- Package READMEs document model, token, and KV-cache effects using the [canonical Model Experience format](../docs/cookbook/adding-a-package.md#4-write-the-package-readme).
- Package READMEs put durable consumer gaps and non-obvious maintainer constraints under `## Known Limitations and Deferred Work`; ordinary cleanup stays in its TODO or Agent Note. Packages with none use a justified [allowlist entry](../scripts/verify-package-readme-limitations.ts) ([rationale](../.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-07-10-readme-known-limitations-gate.md)).

12	import type { Agent, AgentOptions } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent'
13	import type { Branded } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-brand'
14	import type { ContentBlock } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm'
15	import type { SessionEvent, SessionId } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-session'
16	import type { ObjectJsonSchema, ToolRestriction } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools'
17	import type { SubagentDescriptorData } from './descriptor.ts'
18	
19	/** Identifies one accepted subagent run across its lifecycle event pair. */
20	export type SubagentRunId = Branded<'SubagentRunId'>
21	
22	/**
23	 * Brand a string as a {@link SubagentRunId}.
24	 * @param id - the raw run id.
25	 * @returns the same string, branded.
26	 */
27	export function SubagentRunId(id: string): SubagentRunId {
28	  return id as SubagentRunId
29	}
30	
31	/**
32	 * Observe-only identifying detail for a published subagent run, carried by
33	 * `subagent/start`. One-shot runs and continuable Activation epochs share this
34	 * payload, so an observer sees the same vocabulary for both.
35	 */
36	export interface SubagentRunInfo {
37	  /** Unique identity shared with the paired terminal event. */
38	  readonly runId: SubagentRunId
39	  /**
40	   * Provider name recorded when the child was first created. The provider may
41	   * be absent when an accepted one-shot run becomes ready or a persisted
42	   * Activation cold-resumes, because neither lifecycle depends on continued
43	   * registration.
44	   */
45	  readonly provider: string
46	  /** The child agent's id. */
47	  readonly id: SessionId
48	  /** Snapshot of whether `SubagentRun.localAgent` was present when start fulfilled. */
49	  readonly local: boolean
50	}
51	
52	/**
53	 * Observe-only outcome detail for a settled subagent run, carried by
54	 * `subagent/end` and paired with one {@link SubagentRunInfo} by `runId`.
55	 */
56	export interface SubagentRunEndInfo {
57	  /** Unique identity shared with the paired start event. */
58	  readonly runId: SubagentRunId
59	  /** The same provider name carried by the paired start event. */
60	  readonly provider: string
61	  /** The child agent's id. */
62	  readonly id: SessionId
63	  /** Snapshot of whether `SubagentRun.localAgent` was present when start fulfilled. */
64	  readonly local: boolean
65	  /** The terminal stop reason. */
66	  readonly stopReason: SubagentResult['stopReason']
67	  /**
68	   * The child's final assistant output, selected by the same rule as
69	   * {@link SubagentResult.output}; absent on infrastructure rejection or when
70	   * the child produced none.
71	   */
72	  readonly lastAssistantMessage?: ContentBlock[]
73	}
74	
75	/**
76	 * Which START-TIME features a provider supports. Checked by the service before delegating to
77	 * {@link SubagentProvider.start}: a request that needs a capability the chosen provider lacks
78	 * is rejected with a typed error rather than accepted-then-ignored (the "fail loud, no silent
79	 * degradation" rule). These flags describe the ONE-SHOT
80	 * {@link SubagentProvider.start} path, where the provider composes the child;
81	 * continuable children are composed by the continuation manager itself and are
82	 * gated by {@link SubagentProvider.prepareContinuable} instead. Each flag
83	 * corresponds one-to-one to a {@link SubagentStartRequest} option: `depthLimit`
84	 * to `maxDepth`; the other names match.
85	 */
86	export interface SubagentCapabilities {
87	  readonly outputSchema: boolean
88	  readonly depthLimit: boolean
89	  readonly toolFilter: boolean
90	  readonly persona: boolean
91	}
92	
93	/**
94	 * What a caller asks for when starting a ONE-SHOT subagent. The tool layer
95	 * builds this from the model's `{ description, prompt }` plus its own config;
96	 * the service validates {@link SubagentCapabilities} against the named provider
97	 * and resolves the durable descriptor before dispatching to
98	 * {@link SubagentProvider.start}.
99	 */
100	export interface SubagentStartRequest {
101	  /** Optional short display label persisted with a session-backed child. */
102	  readonly label?: string
103	  /** Content delivered as the child's user message. */
104	  readonly prompt: ContentBlock[]
105	  /**
106	   * The spawning agent. In-process providers derive workspace, lineage, and
107	   * delegation depth from its durable session state. ACP reads only its cwd,
108	   * and only when no deployment `cwd` override is configured.
109	   */
110	  readonly parent: Agent
111	  /**
112	   * Cancellation signal from the spawning context (the tool's `exec.signal`).
113	   * This is the canonical cancellation channel both before and after startup:
114	   * a provider rejects `start()` after cleaning partial resources when it
115	   * fires before the run is published, and cancels the published run's
116	   * remaining turn work when it fires afterward.
117	   */
118	  readonly signal: AbortSignal
119	  readonly agentOptions?: AgentOptions
120	  /**
121	   * Object-rooted JSON Schema within `assertObjectJsonSchema`'s enforced subset. Start rejects
122	   * unsupported schemas or providers without the capability. Data must be plain host-realm JSON;
123	   * a successful child returns the matching value as {@link SubagentResult.structured}.
124	   */
125	  readonly outputSchema?: ObjectJsonSchema
126	  /**
127	   * Optional absolute delegation-depth cap for the child being started: its
128	   * computed depth must be less than or equal to this non-negative safe
129	   * integer. Requires {@link SubagentCapabilities.depthLimit}; rejected at
130	   * start otherwise.
131	   */
132	  readonly maxDepth?: number
133	  /**
134	   * Optional child tool scoping. Requires {@link SubagentCapabilities.toolFilter};
135	   * rejected at start otherwise. In-process backends apply it as a scoped
136	   * `tools.restrict()` in the child's creation window: the named tools vanish
137	   * from the child's prompt AND refuse to execute (one visibility), with loud
138	   * unknown-name validation.
139	   */
140	  readonly toolFilter?: ToolRestriction
141	  /**
142	   * Optional per-child persona. Requires {@link SubagentCapabilities.persona};
143	   * rejected at start otherwise. In-process backends register it as a scoped
144	   * `deployment:persona` section on the child, SHADOWING the deployment's
145	   * persona for this child alone — same template semantics as the deployment
146	   * persona (strict `{{…}}` interpolation against the registered variables).
147	   */
148	  readonly persona?: string
149	}
150	
151	/**
152	 * Provider-facing one-shot request after {@link SubagentRuntime.start} resolves
153	 * the durable child descriptor.
154	 */
155	export interface ResolvedSubagentStartRequest extends SubagentStartRequest {
156	  /** Detached descriptor a session-backed provider persists in the child log. */
157	  readonly descriptor: SubagentDescriptorData
158	}
159	
160	/**
161	 * What the continuation manager asks a provider for while materializing one
162	 * continuable child's FIRST activation. The manager has already reserved the
163	 * durable child identity and owns every later operation, so this request
164	 * carries only what distinguishes a fresh child from one seeded with parent
165	 * history.
166	 */
167	export interface ContinuableCreateRequest {
168	  /** The reserved durable child session id, for provider diagnostics. */
169	  readonly sessionId: SessionId
170	  /** The delegating parent agent whose history a seeding provider reads. */
171	  readonly parent: Agent
172	  /**
173	   * Caller cancellation, which owns preparation only until the manager accepts
174	   * the initial prompt into the child's inbox.
175	   */
176	  readonly signal: AbortSignal
177	}
178	
179	/**
180	 * A provider's detached contribution to one continuable child's creation. This
181	 * is DATA, never a capability: it carries no Agent, `AgentHandle`, prompt
182	 * delivery, result, disposal, or resume operation, because the continuation
183	 * manager owns the child's whole lifecycle after preparation.
184	 */
185	export interface ContinuableCreateSpec {
186	  /**
187	   * Completed-turn prefix of the parent's log to seed the child session with,
188	   * or absent for a fresh child. Same durable contract as
189	   * `CreateAgentOptions.seed`: contiguous from seq 0, lossless JSON, balanced.
190	   */
191	  readonly seed?: readonly SessionEvent[]
192	}
193	
194	/**
195	 * Why a subagent run ended. Merge-extensible (a backend may add variants);
196	 * consumers branch on the known cases and fall through `default`. The known
197	 * cases mirror the harness turn-end vocabulary so the tool layer can map a
198	 * non-`completed` result to an `isError` tool result.
199	 */
200	export interface SubagentStopReasonMap {
201	  /** The child finished its turn normally. */
202	  completed: 'completed'
203	  /** Cancelled through the request signal or disposal. */
204	  aborted: 'aborted'
205	  /** Model or transport failure. */
206	  error: 'error'
207	  /** The child hit its token ceiling before finishing. */
208	  'max-tokens': 'max-tokens'
209	  /** The child declined the task. */
210	  refusal: 'refusal'
211	}
212	
213	/** The union over {@link SubagentStopReasonMap} — widens automatically as backends merge in variants. */
214	export type SubagentStopReason = SubagentStopReasonMap[keyof SubagentStopReasonMap]
215	
216	/**
217	 * The terminal outcome of a subagent run, resolved by {@link SubagentRun.result}.
218	 */
219	export interface SubagentResult {
220	  /**
221	   * The child's final assistant output is the content of its last non-empty
222	   * assistant message. Empty-content messages, including usage-only messages,
223	   * are skipped. Without a non-empty message, the output is its accumulated
224	   * assistant text stream, or `[]` when the child produced neither.
225	   */
226	  readonly output: ContentBlock[]
227	  /**
228	   * The structured result after a requested `outputSchema` was successfully
229	   * satisfied. Requesting a schema does not guarantee presence: a provider can
230	   * end with `stopReason: 'error'` when the child fails or finishes without a
231	   * valid capture. The structured value is validated against the requested
232	   * output schema by the provider; `unknown` here because the seam is
233	   * schema-agnostic.
234	   */
235	  readonly structured?: unknown
236	  /** Why the run ended. A non-`completed` reason means `output` may be partial. */
237	  readonly stopReason: SubagentStopReason
238	}
239	
240	/**
241	 * ONE-SHOT child handle returned after publication. Prompt submission, turn
242	 * work, and infrastructure faults after that boundary belong to {@link result}.
243	 * Consumers await that result and must always {@link dispose} to cancel
244	 * remaining work and reach quiescence. A run is one disposable foreground
245	 * delegation with one result; continuable conversations have no run — the
246	 * continuation manager holds their `AgentHandle` directly and orders every
247	 * turn through the child's own inbox.
248	 */
249	export interface SubagentRun {
250	  /**
251	   * Parent-scoped run id. For a local run, this MUST equal the published child
252	   * session id, whose `parentSession` records `request.parent.session.id`; a
253	   * remote provider mints an id unique in the parent namespace.
254	   */
255	  readonly id: SessionId
256	  /**
257	   * The exact published in-process child, or `undefined` for a remote run.
258	   * When present, its id is {@link id}; the provider retains no ownership
259	   * implication beyond the run's ordinary {@link dispose} contract.
260	   */
261	  readonly localAgent: Agent | undefined
262	  /**
263	   * Resolves with the child's terminal {@link SubagentResult} when the run
264	   * settles. Does NOT reject on a child-level failure — a model/transport
265	   * failure resolves with `stopReason: 'error'` so the consumer maps it to an
266	   * `isError` tool result. Rejects on an infrastructure fault the seam cannot
267	   * represent as a stop reason.
268	   */
269	  readonly result: Promise<SubagentResult>
270	  /**
271	   * Cancel remaining work, reach child quiescence, and release resources.
272	   * Idempotent.
273	   */
274	  dispose(): Promise<void>
275	}
276	
277	/**
278	 * One registered transport for running child agents. Providers are trusted
279	 * same-process implementations; callers treat descriptors and returned values
280	 * as borrowed immutable data. The service may call one provider concurrently
281	 * for distinct children. Providers isolate operation-local mutable state; a
282	 * shared capacity controller may delay an operation but must not couple its
283	 * settlement or cleanup to a sibling.
284	 */
285	export interface SubagentProvider {
286	  /** Unique registry name (e.g. `spawn`, `fork`, `acp`). */
287	  readonly name: string
288	  /** The start-time features this provider supports (see {@link SubagentCapabilities}). */
289	  readonly capabilities: SubagentCapabilities
290	  /**
291	   * Whether the child sees the parent's completed-turn prefix. This is descriptive, not a
292	   * service-validated start capability: the model-facing tool derives truthful wording from it.
293	   * It says nothing about tool registration, injected services, or authority inheritance.
294	   */
295	  readonly inheritsParentContext: boolean
296	  /**
297	   * Establish a ONE-SHOT child and return its handle after publication.
298	   * The service has already validated that every requested start-time
299	   * capability is supported and resolved `request.descriptor`, so a
300	   * session-backed implementation appends that descriptor inside the child's
301	   * initial turn. Before fulfillment, the provider owns setup and cleans any
302	   * unpublished partial resources before rejecting. Ownership transfers on
303	   * fulfillment; subsequent turn or infrastructure failure settles through
304	   * the returned run. Distinct starts may overlap; cancellation, failure,
305	   * result settlement, and disposal remain independent for each run.
306	   */
307	  start(request: ResolvedSubagentStartRequest): Promise<SubagentRun>
308	  /**
309	   * OPTIONAL (continuable-creation capability): contribute the detached
310	   * creation inputs that distinguish this provider's continuable children —
311	   * only whether the child session is seeded with parent history. Method
312	   * presence IS the capability: the service rejects continuable starts on
313	   * providers without it, while a provider that has it may still serve
314	   * ordinary one-shot delegations.
315	   *
316	   * This is the provider's ONLY participation in a continuable child. The
317	   * continuation manager owns identity reservation, composition, Agent
318	   * creation, prompt delivery, cold resume, ownership, and disposal, so a
319	   * provider never sees the child's Agent, handle, turns, or teardown.
320	   * Distinct preparations may overlap; each follows its own signal and returns
321	   * data belonging only to `request.sessionId`.
322	   */
323	  prepareContinuable?(request: ContinuableCreateRequest): Promise<ContinuableCreateSpec>
324	}
